insights.insight: At 148 sats (~$0.10) per verified receipt versus $5–$150 CPA for modeled attribution, the cost delta is structural, not incremental — the receipt is the conversion event, not a signal inferred from one.

With Chrome deprecating cookies and fingerprinting increasingly blocked, the ad stack has no cross-site primitive left that produces a verified purchase — only signals that infer one; 6,372 cryptographically signed receipts represent what the stack cannot produce.

Grocery, dining, and gas account for 56% of verified receipts in the trailing 14-day window — the highest-frequency, hardest-to-attribute categories in any brand's media mix are where verified purchase data is accumulating fastest.

The unresolved 'Unknown' store category carries a $107 average basket — nearly double any classified category — suggesting large-ticket purchases are being captured but not yet surfaced, a quality gap that understates the protocol's coverage of high-value transactions.

insights.topic: Growth structure: velocity below 1.0x, acceleration above 1.0x
insights.insight: Raw receipt volume remains suppressed week-over-week, but the growth rate itself is compounding at 1.005x for six consecutive cycles — the system is building throughput capacity faster than current volume reflects.

19 metros added in social-graph pulses rather than paid campaigns — five consecutive cycles each adding 7–9 new CBSAs — indicates organic adoption propagation, which is relevant to brands modeling where verified purchase coverage will appear next.
